scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): a two-view response that grants some engagement value while arguing entertainment undermines journalism's mission; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: The news today often competes with films and games for our limited attention.
Some believe journalism should make news entertaining to keep the public engaged, while others believe this undermines the true mission of journalism.
I lean toward the view that entertainment undermines journalism, though I accept that some engagement is necessary.

sections.role: Body 1 — Why some engagement has value

sentences.text: First, there is real value in making the news engaging enough to reach people.
News that no one reads or watches cannot inform anyone at all.
For example, a lively report can draw people to an important issue they would otherwise ignore.
This shows that some engagement can actually help journalism do its job.
Clear, interesting storytelling can make difficult topics easier to understand.
Reaching a wide audience is part of how journalism serves the public.
To this extent, making news engaging has genuine value.

sections.role: Body 2 — Why entertainment undermines the mission

sentences.text: Second, however, making news entertaining can seriously undermine its real mission.
When news chases excitement, it may favour shocking stories over important ones.
Consider a channel that covers a celebrity scandal at length while ignoring a serious crisis.
Such choices show that entertainment can crowd out the truth people need to know.
Turning news into a show can also tempt journalists to exaggerate or distort the facts.
The mission of journalism is to inform honestly, not merely to amuse.
Entertainment, then, must never be allowed to replace the search for truth.
In conclusion, making the news engaging can help journalism reach and inform the public.
But entertainment undermines journalism when it replaces important truth with mere amusement.
The best journalism keeps people engaged while always putting honest, important information first.
